description:
## Why

Every JMAP method call includes an accountId. Currently this is ignored and all requests operate on the singleton user. With multiuser, the server must verify the authenticated user owns the accountId in the request, and return accountNotFound or forbidden for requests targeting another user's account.

## What

In the JMAP dispatch layer (post stoa-vlhpg integration, the jmap-server Dispatcher), extract the accountId from each method call argument before dispatching. Resolve accountId → user_id and verify it matches the authenticated CallerCtx user_id. Return JmapError::AccountNotFound if the account does not exist, JmapError::Forbidden if it exists but belongs to a different user.

Shared accounts (e.g. a shared mailbox visible to multiple users) are out of scope for v1. Every account is personal and owned by exactly one user.

## Acceptance

- Requests with the correct accountId for the authenticated user succeed
- Requests with another user's accountId return accountNotFound or forbidden (matching jmap_auth_cross_account.rs test expectations)
- Requests with a malformed accountId return accountNotFound
- The existing jmap_auth_cross_account.rs tests pass
notes: The existing crates/mail/tests/jmap_auth_cross_account.rs already tests cross-account rejection. Make sure those tests drive this implementation rather than being worked around.
title: JMAP request routing validates accountId ownership
